thread:
ana: Quick heads-up — saw a regression after the kernel selector tweak that prefers the new int8_generic fallback for AWQ Qwen builds. p50 for the 2-512 seq bucket jumped from ~28ms -> ~62ms on the same infra. Traces attached below.

perf-bot: Profiling summary: GPU stalls at token 2-6, KV eviction spikes around seq > 128, scheduling jitter correlated with prefetch window. (full flamegraphs linked) :mag: 

mohit: Can you paste the exact command/config you used to repro? also which commit changed the selector?

ana: Repro command and minimal logs:

```
# repro profile run
./run_profile --model qwen-12b-awq --kernels=auto --batch-size-hint=4 \
  --prefetch=adaptive --rope-scale=1.0 --prompt-calib=prompts/long-form-calib.json \
  --profile-output=/tmp/qwen_awq_prefetch.pb

# relevant log excerpt
[2026-02-11T22:01:12Z] batcher: slot_wait=1.2ms schedule_delay=0.0ms
[2026-02-11T22:01:12Z] kvcache: evict_count=721 miss_rate=0.18
[2026-02-11T22:01:12Z] kernel_selector: selected=int8_generic (fallback), expected=fused_kv_prefetch
[2026-02-11T22:01:12Z] kernel_runtime: kernel_launch=8.3ms kernel_exec=41.7ms
```

jamie: Interesting — the selector change was rolled in by the last runtime PR (a0b9f3c). It lowered the heuristics weight for fused_kv_prefetch when AWQ calibration flags are present, because of a correctness concern. Maybe that heuristic is too aggressive for mixed-length traffic.

mohit: Do we have calibration prompt differences? AWQ calibration often uses long-form Q&A which can shift RoPE effective scale. If the kernel chooser looks only at quant metadata and sequence length distribution, it might mispredict.

ana: Right. The calibration set for this build included the long-form prompts/long-form-calib.json (mostly doc-level QA, average tokens ~720). That pushed our kv-prefetch budget to assume lots of long context, which triggered more aggressive evictions for short-burst requests. On the timeline the evictions cause extra memcpy + fallback kernel usage.

jamie: Can you share the flamegraph link and the kernel hitrates?

ana: Flamegraphs: https://internal.redwood/prof/qwen-awq/prefetch-wave-1765432100 (read-only)
Kernel hit rates (sample window): fused_kv_prefetch: 12%, int8_generic: 74%, rope-optimized: 14%

mohit: Mixtral builds didn't show this because their kernel path still uses fused_kv_prefetch by default; we never lowered that weight for mixtral. So model-specific default matters. Qwen has different head/kv dims and RoPE handling which interacts badly here.

jamie: Hypothesis: our selector math treats head_dim equivalently across families; for Qwen the kv_dim/head_dim ratio and RoPE scale cause the prefetch heuristic to underestimate memory pressure, so it prefers the generic int8 kernel which has worse runtime for short bursts. It explains the p50 jump.

ana: Quick experiment notes: switching prefetch to `kv-warm` (static warmup) or forcing `fused_kv_prefetch` reduces p50 back to ~30ms at the cost of a small steady-state memory bump. Also reducing the adaptive prefetch window from 128 -> 64 tokens eliminates the eviction spike in our traces.

mohit: Suggestion: change selector weighting to prefer fused_kv_prefetch when either (model_family == "qwen") OR (rope_scale != 1.0) OR (kv_dim / head_dim > 1.0). Minimal patch: bump fused_kv_prefetch_score += 0.2 for those cases.

jamie: +1. Also add a guard in the adaptive prefetcher so it clips evict_count growth per-request: if evict_count increases > X within Y tokens, temporarily reduce prefetch aggressiveness. That would be a low-risk mitigation.

ana: I'll prototype two things: (1) quick selector patch to bias fused_kv_prefetch for qwen/rope!=1; (2) adaptive clip for eviction growth. Will run canary on dedicated pool.

mohit: For the AWQ side, can we try re-running calibration with a mixed prompt set (short+long) to see if AWQ calibration artifacts go away? Might be an orthogonal fix.

ana: Good call — I have a mixed-calib file ready. Running that now and will post results.

taylor: If the selector patch is small, let's ship it behind a runtime flag so we can toggle quickly. We should also add an e2e perf test: run 1000 short-burst requests and assert p50 < 40ms for qwen-awq on baseline infra.

ana: Will do. Plan: patch behind flag -> run canary w/ mixed-calib -> run e2e perf -> if green, flip flag for broader rollout.
